The spiders were hidden inside dirty socks contained in three suitcases carried by two Germans and a Polish citizen, the National Forestry and Wildlife Service (SERFOR) told Agence France-Presse on Thursday.

rfi.title: Mass protests sweep France as workers and students demand higher pay and funding
rfi.description: Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Thursday as workers, students and pensioners joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations demanding higher wages, action on the cost of living and better public services. Nearly 1.6 million people joined the marches, including 350,000 in Paris, the CGT union said. The Interior Ministry gave a much lower nationwide estimate of around 600,000.

rfi.title: ‘We’ll get them’: Macron’s private comments on rivals revealed in new book
rfi.description: Private messages exchanged between French President Emmanuel Macron and journalist Françoise Degois over two years have been published in a new book, revealing his views on political rivals, the rise of the far right and his own leadership. The president reportedly learnt of the book’s existence just three days before its release.

rfi.title: Unicef warns attacks on water supply in conflict zones have tripled in five years
rfi.description: Attacks damaging or destroying water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, Unicef warned on Thursday, leaving millions of children increasingly exposed to disease, malnutrition and violence.

rfi.title: Republican losses show Trump is 'not necessarily the best person to latch on to'
rfi.description: The Democrats’ takeover of the United States Congress sets the stage for a showdown with President Donald Trump, but is unlikely to change his approach to foreign affairs, including the war with Iran, says political scientist Eduardo Gamarra. Speaking to RFI, the Florida International University professor says the party now faces a choice: whether to spend their time investigating the president, or seek compromises on the country’s most pressing problems.

rfi.title: French prosecutors investigate €100m cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel banking group
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a sophisticated cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa involving fraudulent transfers estimated at around €100 million, as the Brittany-based banking group races to recover the stolen funds.

rfi.title: MPs unanimously reject 2027 French budget as political deadlock continues
rfi.description: France's National Assembly has overwhelmingly rejected the government's draft budget for 2027 after MPs from across the political spectrum voted against a heavily amended version of the legislation, sending the bill to the Senate in its original form and setting the stage for another round of difficult negotiations.

rfi.title: Corruption in Kenya taking massive toll on economic growth, warns World Bank
rfi.description: Corruption is costing Kenya billions of dollars each year in lost revenue, inflated business costs, and lost earnings for workers, while taking a huge toll on investment and economic growth, the World Bank said in a report published Wednesday.

rfi.title: South Africa votes in local elections as growing anger threatens ANC
rfi.description: South Africans queued from early on Wednesday to vote in municipal elections, with anger over corruption, crime and failing public services threatening to inflict fresh losses on the African National Congress.

rfi.title: Democratic midterm wins threaten data centre boom in key US states
rfi.description: Strong wins for Democratic candidates threaten the prospects for energy-hungry data centres in key states in the United States, and could slow the AI rollout that has driven Wall Street over the past four years.

rfi.title: French judges open inquiry into allegation of Israeli war crime
rfi.description: French judges have opened a judicial investigation into a complaint of an alleged war crime, following an Israeli strike on a residential building in Beirut in November 2024, it emerged on Tuesday.

rfi.title: PSG coach  Enrique hails 'sensational' Champions League win at Villarreal
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain head coach Luis Enrique on Wednesday hailed his team's performance as sensational after they blazed past Villarreal 6-0 to maintain their perfect start to the defence of their Champions League title.

rfi.title: United Nations confirms end of Western Sahara peacekeeping mission
rfi.description: The United Nations has confirmed it has begun the process of ending its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, after Russia and the United States vetoed each other's draft resolutions on extending the 35-year-old deployment.

rfi.title: Nine out of 10 crimes against journalists go unpunished, Unesco says
rfi.description: Monday marks the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists – chosen in memory of Ghislaine Dupont and Claude Verlon, two journalists from Radio France Internationale who were murdered in Mali on 2 November, 2013. According to a report by Unesco, attacks and harassment targeting the press continue to go largely unpunished in Africa and across the globe.

rfi.title: Calls mount to ban French TV channel following racist killing
rfi.description: A petition urging that a French television channel be taken off air gained traction on Monday, after accusations that far-right views it aired contributed to the racist killing of a black man.

rfi.title: Nigerian health chiefs confirm negative results in Ebola cases
rfi.description: Health authorities investigating two suspected Ebola cases in north-eastern Nigeria ​confirmed on Monday that both samples were negative after ‌two rounds of testing.

rfi.title: France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attack on police
rfi.description: France has launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors told AFP on Sunday.

euronews.title: West Bank: Palestinians harvest olives under Israeli military restrictions
euronews.description: Palestinian farmers in the occupied West Bank have been allowed limited access to their olive groves under Israeli military restrictions. Many found damaged trees, while soldiers fired tear gas near the harvest.

euronews.title: Spain: Zelensky urges Latin America to help repair Ukraine's power grid
euronews.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has appealed to Spain and Latin American countries for urgent help repairing Ukraine's damaged energy infrastructure. He also met King Felipe VI during the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid.

euronews.title: Paraguayan president resigns amid bank collapse leaving 3M people without access to bank accounts
euronews.description: Santiago Peña resigned as president of Paraguay amid the Ueno Bank crisis and was later impeached over an alleged conflict of interest. Vice President Pedro Alliana will take office, while millions of Paraguayans wait to recover their deposits.

euronews.title: British comedian Russell Brand found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults by London jury
euronews.description: Russell Brand was convicted of four sexual offences, one rape and three sexual assaults, involving four women between 2005 and 2009 in different locations.

euronews.title: Greece: Students march in Athens demanding more education funding
euronews.description: Thousands of pupils, students and teachers marched through central Athens on Thursday in a nationwide push for better-funded schools, joining a protest wave that has spread from France across southern Europe.

euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 5th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: World Investment Forum in Doha examines what attracts investment and what holds it back
euronews.description: Foreign investment remains concentrated in relatively few countries, while others struggle to attract funding. At the World Investment Forum in Doha, governments and businesses discussed how more economies could benefit and turn investment into jobs.

euronews.title: Putin seizes Russian operations of cigarette giant Japan Tobacco International
euronews.description: The decree transferred JTI’s four factories, around 4,000 employees and roughly 40% of the Russian cigarette market to a state-linked holding company. The latest seizure added to a list that includes Nestlé, Auchan, Leroy Merlin and Metro.

euronews.title: Everyday people: Jeans, plastic and paper among Met Gala's surprising new fashion themes
euronews.description: The 2027 Met Gala will celebrate the potential of everyday objects and materials, from jeans and T-shirts to paper and plastic. The accompanying exhibition next spring will explore how designers transform ordinary items into works of art.

euronews.title: EU plans to deliver 'AI literacy' certificates to students
euronews.description: The European Union has announced that it has started to work on creating a certificate for "AI literacy" that would be delivered to successful 15-year-old students for the next school year.

euronews.title: Italian PM slams EU’s fragmented approach to Ukraine peace talks
euronews.description: In a letter to European Council President António Costa, Giorgia Meloni says multiple negotiating formats are making Europe “less credible” to end the war.

euronews.title: Protesters across Europe to call for freeze on energy hungry data centres
euronews.description: After US midterms, European campaigners bring the data centre backlash to Europe.

euronews.title: Fireworks may be fun, but their health risks are not
euronews.description: Fireworks may be a staple of celebrations, but their health risks are prompting experts to call for stricter regulations and greater public awareness.

euronews.title: Ueno Bank collapse in Paraguay prompts President Santiago Peña to resign
euronews.description: The accounting black hole at Ueno Bank wipes out public funds, leaves thousands without access to their deposits and drives Paraguay into its worst institutional crisis in years.

euronews.title: France: Up to 55,000 march in Lyon amid clashes and tear gas
euronews.description: Tens of thousands marched through Lyon area during a nationwide strike over wages and purchasing power. Police charged demonstrators and used tear gas as clashes erupted along the protest route.

euronews.title: More flights, fewer emissions: this country’s aviation challenge
euronews.description: Azerbaijan is working to reduce aviation emissions while handling growing air traffic. From fuel-efficient aircraft and airport carbon accreditation to digital air navigation, the industry is exploring ways to make flying more sustainable.

euronews.title: Inside New Tashkent, Uzbekistan's planned city for two million people
euronews.description: Nearly 7,000 apartments are complete, three ministries already operate there and university facilities have opened. Projects worth $50bn (€44.8bn) are planned for the first phase, with a FIFA-standard stadium under construction and a metro connection proposed.

euronews.title: Bank of England raises key interest rate for first time in over 3 years
euronews.description: The Bank of England has raised interest rates to 4% as it tries to curb rising prices fuelled by the Iran war.

lemonde.title: A Wall Street, la victoire démocrate aux midterms a fait exploser la bulle de l’IA
lemonde.description: Le Nasdaq, l’indice qui regroupe de nombreuses valeurs technologiques, a perdu plus de 5,5 %, jeudi 5 novembre. Les résultats des élections américaines de mi-mandat accentuent la défiance envers la plupart des valeurs liées à l’intelligence artificielle et aux data centers.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, grève du 5 novembre : entre 575 000 et 1,6 million de manifestants en France jeudi, une « conférence sociale » avec les syndicats et le patronat prévue à Matignon lundi
lemonde.description: La CGT estime que les mobilisations ont réuni près de 1,6 million de personnes, dont 350 000 à Paris. De son côté, le ministère de l’intérieur a évalué à 575 000 le nombre de manifestants en France, dont 65 000 dans la capitale.

lemonde.title: Le ciel européen en état d’alerte après des menaces visant une vingtaine de vols commerciaux
lemonde.description: Plusieurs pays, dont la France, ont dû mobiliser leur armée de l’air pour escorter des avions de ligne menacés par des alertes à la bombe. Une vingtaine de vols étaient concernés, ce qui laisse supposer une opération coordonnée.

lemonde.title: Israël : Gadi Eisenkot, l’ancien chef d’état-major israélien, en bonne position pour remplacer Benyamin Nétanyahou à la tête du gouvernement
lemonde.description: Gadi Eisenkot a été désigné par les dirigeants de six partis, représentant une majorité des sièges à la Knesset, comme le candidat le plus légitime pour former un nouveau gouvernement. Le chef de l’Etat, Isaac Herzog, annoncera sa décision dimanche.

lemonde.title: Vanté par Donald Trump, l’accord américano-russe sur le gazole bat de l’aile
lemonde.description: Plusieurs navires russes chargés de gazole destiné au marché américain ont brusquement changé de cap en haute mer, ces derniers jours. Craignant les risques réputationnels et les sanctions, les entreprises américaines rechignent à en acheter.

lemonde.title: En Irak, petites mains et figures du djihadisme français passent en jugement
lemonde.description: Parmi les 47 ressortissants français transférés depuis la Syrie et jugés par la justice irakienne à Bagdad pour appartenance à l’organisation Etat islamique figurent des vétérans du djihadisme hexagonal, à l’image de Thomas Collange.

lemonde.title: Coalition de Glucksmann à Lisnard : l’idée d’Emmanuel Macron ne trouve pas d’écho, même chez ses héritiers
lemonde.description: Mercredi, le président de la République a estimé, devant des visiteurs, que la social-démocratie, le centre et la droite devraient se rassembler dans une grande coalition. Une hypothèse accueillie avec froideur par les prétendants à sa succession.

lemonde.title: Au procès de l’explosion de la rue de Trévise, la notion d’urgence des travaux à réaliser en question
lemonde.description: D’anciens salariés du syndic Cipa ont été entendus comme témoins, jeudi, au tribunal judiciaire de Paris. Au cœur des interrogations, le fait que cette société n’avait pas recouru à la procédure d’urgence qui lui aurait permis de faire réparer des fuites ayant joué un rôle crucial dans la catastrophe de janvier 2019.

lemonde.title: Sébastien Lecornu exhorte les banques à financer les candidats à l’élection présidentielle
lemonde.description: Le premier ministre a envoyé deux nouveaux courriers aux banques françaises. Celles-ci plaident pour une solution impliquant des établissements financiers détenus directement ou indirectement par l’Etat.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la trêve d’Olechky prouve que « quand Poutine le veut, les combats s’arrêtent », estime Volodymyr Zelensky
lemonde.description: « Il en va de même pour nos compatriotes détenus en captivité en Russie. Quand Poutine le veut, ils rentrent chez eux. Et il en va de même pour nos enfants enlevés par la Russie », a ajouté le président ukrainien.

lemonde.title: Le nouveau TGV de la SNCF, plus confortable, écologique et modulable, entre enfin en service vendredi
lemonde.description: Après des années de tests et de retards, le premier TGV nouvelle génération de la SNCF prend le départ de Paris, vendredi matin, pour Marseille avec de nombreuses innovations. Les nouvelles rames remplaceront progressivement, sur dix ans environ, le parc existant.

lemonde.title: Le lycée Françoise à Tournefeuille, près de Toulouse, victime d’une attaque, d’un incendie et de dégradations
lemonde.description: Tôt le matin, jeudi 5 novembre, une trentaine d’individus cagoulés ont pénétré dans l’établissement scolaire. Les dégâts sont importants et les réactions indignées.

lemonde.title: Etats-Unis : Google accusé d’avoir laissé son assistant IA Gemini aider une collégienne à planifier un suicide
lemonde.description: Avant que ses parents n’interviennent, l’adolescente de 13 ans a échangé, à l’aide de l’ordinateur fourni par son école, des milliers de messages avec le modèle phare d’intelligence artificielle du groupe américain, dans lesquels elle décrit son mal-être.

lemonde.title: Dépenses du gouvernement : une étude relève « l’opacité » des rémunérations dans les cabinets ministériels
lemonde.description: Dans une note pour l’Observatoire de l’éthique publique, qu’il préside, l’ancien député René Dosière évalue le « coût du gouvernement Lecornu » à 165,7 millions d’euros en année pleine, soit moins d’un millième des dépenses publiques.

lemonde.title: Le préfet du Rhône interdit une conférence du député LFI Raphaël Arnault vendredi à Villeurbanne
lemonde.description: « Cette mesure a pour objectif de prévenir les risques de troubles à l’ordre public et notamment les affrontements entre des groupuscules radicaux qui revendiquent l’usage de la violence », justifie la préfecture.

lemonde.title: Crise politique au Paraguay après l’annonce de la démission du président Santiago Peña
lemonde.description: Faute de vote au Parlement, M. Peña reste techniquement à la tête de l’Etat mais il est visé par une procédure de destitution. Cette séquence est provoquée par l’éclatement d’une crise bancaire, qui a vu la Banque centrale du Paraguay mettre sous tutelle Ueno, une entité financière revendiquant près de 3 millions de clients.

france24fr.title: Trump vs le Congrès : la bataille des pouvoirs
france24fr.description: Pour ces élections de mi-mandat, le verdict est sans appel : les démocrates sont les grands gagnants. Donald Trump a donc perdu sa majorité au Sénat à la Chambre des représentants. Dès janvier, il va devoir composer avec un Congrès aux mains de l'opposition, une sorte de cohabitation à l'américaine.

france24fr.title: Municipales en Afrique du Sud: l'ANC se dirige vers son pire résultat électoral
france24fr.description: Le Congrès national africain (ANC), à la tête de l'Afrique du Sud depuis 1994, se dirige vers le pire résultat électoral de son histoire, indiquent les scores après dépouillement de la moitié des votes des élections municipales jeudi en fin de journée. Un peu plus d'un électeur sud-africain sur deux s'est déplacé mercredi pour voter aux municipales, a annoncé la commission électorale.

france24fr.title: Grèves et manifestations en France : le pouvoir sous pression ?
france24fr.description: Nouvelle journée de mobilisation à l’appel des organisations syndicales, qui prennent le relai des mouvements des lycéens et étudiants. Parmi les revendications : la revalorisation des salaires, la sauvegarde des services publics et la défense du droit à manifester en soutien à la jeunesse. 600 000 personnes ont battu le pavé partout en France selon le ministère de l'Intérieur, un million 600 000 selon la CGT. Près de 10% des agents de la fonction publique d'État ont participé à la grève. Sébast

france24fr.title: Chaos dans l'espace aérien européen
france24fr.description:
Les alertes à la bombe se multiplient dans le ciel européen. Ce jeudi, un vol Dublin-Rome a été dérouté vers une base militaire française, escorté par deux avions de chasse. Comment les autorités font-elles face à ces menaces ? Ces incidents pourraient-ils s'inscrire dans une stratégie d'attaques hybrides contre l'Europe ?
 
Gérard Feldzer, ancien pilote de ligne et consultant en aéronautique, décrypte les procédures et les enjeux de ces alertes.

france24fr.title: Paraguay : le président Santiago Peña au bord de la destitution sur fond de scandale bancaire
france24fr.description: Dans la foulée d'un scandale bancaire national, le président du Paraguay, Santiago Peña, a annoncé sa démission jeudi, mais restait techniquement à la tête de l'État car le Parlement n'a pas réussi à voter pour l'accepter ou la refuser. Accusé de "mauvais exercice de ses fonctions" et de "conflit d'intérêts", il se prépare à son procès en destitution vendredi.

france24fr.title: COP31: le déficit de financement de l'adaptation est "ahurissant" (ONU)
france24fr.description: Les financements de l'adaptation doivent être multipliés par dix, selon l'ONU. Les Nations Unies viennent de publier un rapport à quelques jours de l'ouverture de la COP31. Son titre: "Sommes-nous prêts? Non". Le message est explicite et appuyé par le secrétaire général des Nations-Unies, Antonio Guterres: "le choix est simple : investir dans l'adaptation aujourd'hui ou payer le prix de la catastrophe demain" a-t-il dit dans une vidéo postée sur Internet.

france24fr.title: Manifestations pour le pouvoir d'achat, défaite de Donald Trump aux élections de mi-mandat
france24fr.description: La journée de mobilisation à l’appel des syndicats et pour le pouvoir d’achat, a réuni 600 000 personnes selon le gouvernement. Les syndicats réclament une hausse significative du SMIC et l’augmentation des salaires. Quels leviers le gouvernement a-t-il pour répondre aux revendications ? Aux Etats-Unis, c’est une autre colère qui s’est exprimée dans les urnes : Donald Trump a subi un revers cinglant aux élections de mi-mandat. Est-ce un échec du populisme ?

france24fr.title: France : manifestations dans plusieurs villes ce 5 novembre
france24fr.description: La CGT a revendiqué jeudi "près de 1,6 million" de manifestants en France, dont 350 000 à Paris, lors d'une journée de mobilisation pour les salaires et les services publics, à l'initiative des syndicats. Le ministère de l'Intérieur a, de son côté, dénombré près de 600 000 participants selon un décompte provisoire. Dans les deux cas, il s'agit de la plus forte mobilisation de cet automne.

france24fr.title: “Rue du Goût Perdu” : la gastronomie pour tous
france24fr.description: Comment rendre la gastronomie accessible à tous ? Avec le projet "Rue du Goût Perdu", deux jeunes cuisiniers organisent des dîners gastronomiques solidaires pour faire découvrir la cuisine et les saveurs d'antan aux habitants de leur quartier.

france24fr.title: Un Airbus A320 Dublin-Rome dérouté vers Évreux à cause d’une alerte à la bombe
france24fr.description: Un airbus A320 reliant Dublin à Rome a été dérouté vers Évreux, en Normandie, à cause d’une alerte à la bombe ce jeudi 5 novembre. Les 157 personnes à bord sont saines et sauves

Espagne : mort du joueur Jesus de Miguel, le football en deuil
france24fr.description: Le gardien du Andorre FC, Jesus Owono, est sorti du silence mercredi 4 novembre en assurant qu'il vivait "les jours les plus difficiles" de sa vie, au lendemain de la mort de l'attaquant de Tenerife Jesus de Miguel, qu'il avait violemment percuté en plein match lundi 2 novembre. Selon la presse espagnole, Owono risque une lourde suspension sportive et pourrait se retrouver devant la justice pour "homicide par négligence". Les précisions de Maude Petit-Jové

france24fr.title: Manifestations contre la vie chère en France : le taux de pauvreté au plus haut
france24fr.description: En France, le taux de pauvreté n’a jamais été aussi haut depuis au moins trente ans. Une situation qui fait partie des enjeux au cœur des mobilisations de ce jeudi 5 novembre. La France comptait 9,8 millions de personnes sous le seuil de pauvreté en 2024 selon l'Insee. Environ 15,5 % de la population française vit chaque mois avec moins de 60 % du revenu médian, soit moins de 1 337 euros pour une personne seule. Les précisions de Ludovic De Foucaud, journaliste à France 24.

france24fr.title: Midterms : le vice-président américain prend ses distances avec Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Le vice-président américain J.D. Vance a pris ⁠mercredi 4 novembre ses distances ​avec la guerre en Iran menée par le président Donald Trump, s'interrogeant sur la pertinence d'une telle décision et imputant au conflit les lourds ​revers subis la veille par les républicains lors des élections de mi-mandat au Congrès. Les précisions de Matthieu Mabin, chroniqueur international à France 24.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : le consensus pro-israélien de l'opinion américaine se fissure
france24fr.description: La victoire du progressiste Abdul El-Sayed aux élections de mi-mandat, après une campagne marquée par ses critiques d'Israël, illustre l'érosion du soutien de l'opinion américaine à l'État hébreu depuis les guerres à Gaza et en Iran. Entre coût de la vie liées aux tensions au Moyen-Orient et aspirations isolationnistes à droite, l'alignement historique des États-Unis sur le gouvernement israélien vacille aussi.

france24fr.title: JOJ : match fou entre le Sénégal et le Panama en futsal
france24fr.description: Les Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse se poursuivent au Sénégal. L'équipe masculine du pays hôte ont créé la sensation en futsal face au Panama. Notre correspondante Sarah Sakho revient sur cette folle rencontre et nous donne les autres temps forts de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Budget 2027 : l'Assemblée nationale rejette à l'unanimité le projet de budget de l'État
france24fr.description: Les députés ont rejeté mercredi 4 novembre en première lecture, et à l'unanimité des votes exprimés, le projet de budget de l'Etat 2027, qui sera donc envoyé dans sa version initiale au Sénat. Après avoir supprimé plusieurs articles-clés du texte gouvernemental, l'Assemblée a rejeté comme l'an dernier la partie "recettes" du texte, avec 458 voix contre, issues de tous les groupes, et deux abstentions au sein du groupe communiste et ultramarin.

france24fr.title: Grèves en France : comment les manifestations sont vues de l'étranger ?
france24fr.description: Les mobilisations aux luttes convergentes s'enchaînent en France depuis des semaines, dépassant parfois les frontières de la France. En Europe, la jeunesse albanaise, italienne et grecque est, elle aussi, sortie dans les rues. À l'échelle internationale, comment ces manifestations sont -elles vues ? Les Fribourgeois renouvellent ce dimanche leurs autorités cantonales. spiegel.title: Großbritannien will Gehaltsangaben in Stellenanzeigen vorschreiben
spiegel.description: Transparente Gehälter sind in vielen Länder ein Tabu. Auch in Stellenanzeigen halten sich Arbeitgeber oft bedeckt. In Großbritannien soll sich das ändern. Profitieren könnte ein bislang oft benachteiligter Teil der Bewerber.

spiegel.title: Audi will geplantes US-Werk in Georgia offenbar noch vergrößern
spiegel.description: In Deutschland droht eine Werkschließung, in den USA erwägt Audi eine milliardenschwere Erweiterung seiner Neubaupläne. So könnten im Bundesstaat Georgia Tausende Arbeitsplätze zusätzlich entstehen.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Trump erklärt sein vergoldetes Oval Office zum Nationaldenkmal
spiegel.description: Das Oval Office platzt vor lauter Gold aus allen Nähten. Und das soll laut Donald Trump auch so bleiben. Mit einem Trick will er künftigen US-Präsidenten – in seinen Worten: »dummen Leuten« – das Umdekorieren vermiesen.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: US-Regierung hält trotz Kriegs an Abschiebeplänen nach Iran fest
spiegel.description: Donald Trump hat Iran wiederholt mit »Vernichtung« gedroht. Das hält seine Regierung aber nicht davon ab, Rückführungen in das Kriegsland anzuschieben. Vor einem US-Bundesgericht fielen deshalb klare Worte.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: 448 Festnahmen bei landesweiten Protesten
spiegel.description: In Frankreich haben vorwiegend junge Menschen abermals für bessere Schulen und gegen Sozialkürzungen protestiert. Es kam zu Gewalt vonseiten der Demonstranten und der Polizei.

spiegel.title: Midterms-Siege der Demokraten: Furcht vor KI-Regulierung lässt US-Tech-Aktien einbrechen
spiegel.description: Nach den US-Zwischenwahlen müssen sich KI-Konzerne wohl auf mehr politischen Gegenwind einstellen. Am Aktienmarkt verlieren deswegen nun die Werte von Chipherstellern deutlich an Wert – in den USA, aber auch in Deutschland.

spiegel.title: Harmeet Dhillon: Trump-Vertraute tritt zurück
spiegel.description: Für ihren Präsidenten bekämpfte sie Eliteuniversitäten und die »Woke-Ideologie« – zumindest bis jetzt: Die Spitzenbeamtin im US-Justizministerium Harmeet Dhillon hat kurz nach den Midterms ihre Kündigung eingereicht.

spiegel.title: Kalifornien: Gouverneur Gavin Newsom wandelt alle 548 Todesurteile im Staat in Haftstrafen um
spiegel.description: In dem Bundesstaat wartet nun niemand mehr auf seine Hinrichtung: Gouverneur Gavin Newsom kippt alle 548 bestehenden Todesurteile in Kalifornien. In einem Brief an die Bürger findet er zudem deutliche Worte über die Todesstrafe.

spiegel.title: Paraguay: Präsident Santiago Peña tritt nach Bankenskandal zurück
spiegel.description: Lange Schlangen vor den Geldautomaten und ein Finanzinstitut in Schieflage: Eine Bankenkrise hat Paraguays Staatschef Peña das Amt gekostet. Kritiker werfen ihm Interessenkonflikte im Umgang mit der Bank vor.

spiegel.title: Midterms in den USA: Die trügerische Freude über Trumps Machtverlust
spiegel.description: Donald Trump verliert die US-Zwischenwahlen. Auch in Ungarn, Brasilien und Serbien scheiterten Rechtspopulisten. Ist das der Anfang vom Ende ihrer weltweiten Erfolgswelle? Hören Sie eine neue Folge von »Mad Kings«.

spiegel.title: Bakterielle Belastung: Pinienkern- und Rindfleischsalami-Produkte werden zurückgerufen
spiegel.description: Wegen möglicher Belastung mit Salmonellen beziehungsweise Coli-Bakterien werden verschiedene Artikel mit Pinienkernen und Rindfleischsalami zurückgeholt. Betroffen sind Produkte von dm, Dennree, Alnatura und der Fleischmarke »Peter Faden«.

spiegel.title: Bundestagsbeschluss: Schlachthöfe werden künftig mit Kameras überwacht
spiegel.description: Tierquälerei-Skandale sind an deutschen Schlachthöfen keine Seltenheit. Der Bundestag hat größere Betriebe nun zur Videoüberwachung verpflichtet. So sollen mehr als 90 Prozent aller Schlachtungen erfasst werden.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz entgleitet die Suche nach einer Bundespräsidentin
spiegel.description: Der Kanzler verrät nicht, wen er für das Bundespräsidentenamt favorisiert. Doch CSU-Kandidatin Ilse Aigner bekommt so viel Unterstützung, dass Friedrich Merz sie kaum noch übergehen kann, ohne Schaden anzurichten.

spiegel.title: NSDAP-Kartei: So forschen Sie nach der Recherche im SPIEGEL-Archiv weiter
spiegel.description: Sie haben die NSDAP-Kartei des SPIEGEL genutzt und fragen sich: Wie forsche ich weiter? Ab 19.30 Uhr beantworten Historiker Johannes Spohr und SPIEGEL-Redakteur Frederik Seeler Ihre Fragen im Livestream.

spiegel.title: Alan Jones ist tot: Nachruf auf den Formel-1-Weltmeister
spiegel.description: Alan Jones fuhr den Williams-Rennstall zum ersten WM-Titel in der Formel 1. Der Australier triumphierte in einem wilden Jahr des Motorsports. Mit 80 Jahren ist er nun gestorben.

spiegel.title: »White Tiger«: Wie Russland mutmaßlich Teenager für Anschläge rekrutiert
spiegel.description: Rekrutiert Russland Teenager im Netz, um Chaos zu verbreiten? Indizien legen das nahe: Brandanschläge, Messerattacken und ein Bündel Rubelscheine.

spiegel.title: Texas: Wie Gina Hinojosa die Republikaner-Hochburg umkrempeln will
spiegel.description: Gina Hinojosa ist für Texas noch wichtiger als der künftige Senator James Talarico: Die neue Gouverneurin will das Geflecht zwischen Republikanern und Oligarchen zerschlagen. Vor allem für Elon Musk könnte sich einiges ändern.

spiegel.title: Israel: Gadi Eisenkot bekommt die meisten Empfehlungen aus dem israelischen Parlament
spiegel.description: Israel sucht weiter nach einer Regierungskoalition. Jetzt haben sich die arabischen Parteien auf die Seite des Oppositionskandidaten geschlagen. Sicherheiten bringt das aber nicht.

elpais.description: El músico odia los protocolos y siempre es capaz de llamar la atención con sus escasas apariciones públicas. Las imágenes con el Papa guardan simbolismo, incluso político justo después de la derrota de Trump en EE UU

elpais.description: Tres de cuatro Estados que llevaron el tema del aborto a las urnas se pronunciaron a favor de garantizar el derecho a la interrupción voluntaria del embarazo

npr.description: On Morning Edition, Pulitzer Prize-winning historian Anne Applebaum breaks down what a Democratic Congress could change about Trump's foreign policy and what remains beyond its power.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

phys-org.title: How mitochondria keep protein production moving
phys-org.description: Researchers at Karolinska Institutet have discovered how a protein called TACO1 helps mitochondria produce proteins when the process encounters difficult sequences. The study, published in Nature Communications, provides new insights into a mechanism that is disrupted in some mitochondrial diseases.

phys-org.title: Research seeks to clarify assisted suicide practices in Germany and inform future regulation
phys-org.description: Assisted suicide is morally and ethically controversial. Public debate on the topic tends to arise primarily when a high-profile case comes to light—as was most recently the case with the famous twins Alice and Ellen Kessler. While assisted suicide is permitted in Germany, it is scarcely regulated by law. Until now, there has been little scientifically validated data on the current practice of assisted suicide.

phys-org.title: Can engineering solve the forever chemical problem?
phys-org.description: Among the technical inquiries spanning topics like cyclodextrin polymers and mass spectrometry that were stacked in Damian Helbling's inbox was a question about four golden retrievers.

phys-org.title: Hidden ecological risk from overlooked invasive crayfish species
phys-org.description: A new study reveals narrow-clawed crayfish, an understudied invasive species in the U.K., to be as aggressive as the well-known signal crayfish.

phys-org.title: Successful restoration of fish migration requires more than fish passes
phys-org.description: The Netherlands is constructing fish passes to make rivers and streams accessible to fish again. But how effective are these structures? New Ph.D. research by Panos Panagiotopoulos of Wageningen University shows that successful fish migration requires more than making individual barriers passable. Maintenance and water management are also crucial.

phys-org.title: Soccer: Opaque club ownership is more likely associated with higher financial and criminal risks
phys-org.description: Who are the ultimate owners of Italian soccer clubs? Where does the money invested in these clubs come from? And what risks lie behind investment funds, fiduciary companies and transnational corporate structures that make it difficult to identify the individuals who ultimately control them?

phys-org.title: How often should you be working at the office? Here's what the research suggests
phys-org.description: Office attendance from Monday to Friday used to be a pretty standard requirement for many jobs. But plenty of employees have now developed a taste for working from home. And in response, some of their employers have started to tighten the rules on hybrid work.

phys-org.title: Chemicals in sewage-based fertilizer may persist in farmland soil for years
phys-org.description: UNSW engineers have identified a number of chemicals that may merit closer scrutiny to ensure water utility companies and regulators can make informed decisions about the management of biosolids.

phys-org.title: Astronomers deliver the sharpest and deepest view yet of the low-frequency radio sky
phys-org.description: Using the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR), an international team led by Leiden University has produced the sharpest and most sensitive radio image of the sky ever made at low radio frequencies. The image reveals almost 63,000 radio sources, such as active galactic nuclei and star-forming galaxies, across a patch of sky about 25 times the area of the full moon. The results have been accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics. The paper is currently available on the arXiv preprint server.

phys-org.title: Children may be missing out on free school meals as families favor private education, study finds
phys-org.description: Children in some of India's poorest families may be missing out on free school meals because the scheme does not match parents' aspirations for their futures, new research has revealed.

phys-org.title: Twisted atomic layers slide spontaneously at room temperature in simulations
phys-org.description: Researchers revealed an ultralow-barrier collective sliding mechanism mediated by domain walls, as well as defect-induced pinning of the sliding motion. They found that twisted bilayer MoS₂ moiré superlattices can undergo spontaneous long-range interlayer sliding at room temperature, while a sulfur-vacancy concentration of only about 0.1% can turn the motion into localized oscillations.

phys-org.title: Climate shapes microbial nitrogen pump in forests, not in farmlands
phys-org.description: Microbes build a long-lived nitrogen reservoir in soil from the remains of dead bacteria and fungi, which cling to minerals and resist decay. The microbial nitrogen pump turns nitrogen taken up by living microbes into this persistent pool, and microbial nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) has long been assumed to regulate this process.

phys-org.title: Societies could lose ability to respond to climate change
phys-org.description: Human societies could lose the ability to respond to worsening climate change, scientists have warned.

phys-org.title: Laser-plasma accelerator could generate bright X-rays for biological imaging, simulations show
phys-org.description: X-rays with wavelengths between approximately 2.3 and 4.4 nanometers, i.e., in the so-called water window, are particularly well suited to examining biological samples in their natural, aqueous environment. To date, however, it has been technically difficult to access this type of radiation at an appropriate quality and intensity, as only free-electron lasers in large-scale accelerator systems are capable of generating it.

phys-org.title: Land plants' closest algal relatives evolved multicellular growth repeatedly, genetic analysis suggests
phys-org.description: What did the algae that gave rise to the first land plants look like? A research team led by the University of Göttingen and including the universities of Maastricht and Innsbruck and Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales has now taken a detailed look at one of the most important groups for answering this question: the Zygnematophyceae, the closest living algal relatives of land plants. phys-org.description: You have probably performed a sandwich assay before, even if you didn't know it. Sandwich assays are the molecular sensing technology behind lateral flow tests like the at-home COVID test. After a sample is dripped onto the test strip, it combines with detector antibodies attached to tiny gold particles, which bind to any viral proteins present. phys-org.title: Underwater cameras can estimate fish weight in real time without generating full depth maps
phys-org.description: Accurate fish-weight estimates can help aquaculture operators manage feeding, monitor growth and plan harvests. However, conventional underwater imaging methods often require substantial computing power and can struggle with reflections, bubbles and turbid water.

phys-org.title: New placenta-on-a-chip model allows engineers to study effects of environmental toxins
phys-org.description: Exposure to toxic metals like cadmium has been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes such as miscarriage, preterm birth and low birth weight. Because these effects are difficult and ethically challenging to study directly in pregnant women, how such exposures affect pregnancy has remained poorly understood.

proj-syn.title: Turning Sub-Saharan Africa’s Cities Into Job Engines

But unlocking urbanization’s potential requires policy guidance and well-planned investment.

proj-syn.title: Why Are Indian Protesters Targeting the Electoral Commission?
proj-syn.description: Following a “special intensive revision” that struck 130 million voters from the electoral rolls, India’s youth have mounted large-scale protests against the Election Commission. Given the convergence of protests with the formal political opposition, the Commission is unlikely to avoid accountability for mass disenfranchisement.

proj-syn.title: Why Aren’t We Investing More in Climate Adaptation?
proj-syn.description: There are many proven ways to protect people and assets from extreme weather, and such measures often prevent economic losses worth many times their cost. But ensuring their implementation requires making them more affordable and creating innovative revenue mechanisms and financing structures.

proj-syn.title: Put the Ocean at the Center of COP31
proj-syn.description: Last year’s UN Climate Change Conference in Belém, Brazil, put forests high on the climate agenda. This month’s UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, can do the same for the ocean, whose warming threatens not just food and energy security but global survival.

proj-syn.title: Who's Winning (and Who's Losing) The Ocean?
proj-syn.description: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Peter Thomson, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Ocean, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as he warns of a “world on fire,” takes governments to task for kowtowing to the oil and gas industry, and explains how we can do better for future generations.

proj-syn.title: The Democrats’ Historic Duty
proj-syn.description: While Democrats have good reason to celebrate their historic midterm victory, their current elation must quickly harden into determination. Fortunately, the field for new ideas, systemic and economic, in the US will be the most open it is likely to be for decades.

proj-syn.title: Dot-Com Lessons for the AI Bubble
proj-syn.description: Anyone who lived through the internet boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s should find the current AI investment cycle worryingly familiar. Heavy reliance on debt means that if investors decide to stop lending into the boom, a financial crisis will be inevitable—and far worse than the subprime-mortgage crisis in 2008.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.

proj-syn.title: The Rise and Fall of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Privacy is not a natural phenomenon, but rather a historical achievement. It emerged after the Reformation and the wars of religion that followed, reached a high point during the Victorian era, and has now been eroding for decades, long before the advent of the digital economy, social media, and AI.

proj-syn.title: Good Institutions Require Good People
proj-syn.description: Well-designed laws, courts, catechisms, extrinsic motives, social approval, and even a few good and decent people are of no avail if too many people do not behave like self-respecting and other-respecting adults. Childish pride and envy, grabbing more of the sweets, Donald Trump-style, do not make for a good society.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchic World Order
proj-syn.description: Today, some 64 heads of state or government are oligarchs, leading countries that together account for some 60% of global GDP. The question is thus no longer whether oligarchs will rule the world, but rather what kind of world they are building.

proj-syn.title: Poland’s Constitutional Civil War
proj-syn.description: Polish right-wing populists recently stormed the country's Constitutional Tribunal, winning applause from the Kremlin and far-right fellow-travelers across Europe. As in other countries, the constitutional tribunal is the institution that distinguishes a proper democracy from a dictatorship making it a target for authoritarians.

proj-syn.title: The Tech Brotherhood Wants Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: After centuries of nation-states, a new form of sovereignty is asserting itself. The small fraternity that controls the major digital platforms has already proven capable of even more intrusive and insidious forms of control than most states can muster.

proj-syn.title: The Far Right’s Vision for Europe
proj-syn.description: In many ways, Europe’s far right has already won, regardless of what happens at the ballot box in the coming months. Its parties may still quarrel among themselves, but they agree on the three big issues that will define much of the European political agenda for years to come.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Bright Future
proj-syn.description: A narrative of European decline has taken hold, and if the EU continues on its current path, it may well materialize. But this is not a foregone conclusion: Europe retains considerable strengths on which it can build as it pursues critical reforms aimed at unleashing innovation.

proj-syn.title: A Debtors’ Club for a Fragmented World
proj-syn.description: The newly created Borrowers’ Platform aims to facilitate knowledge-sharing and capacity-building among debtor countries, while amplifying their voices in global financial circles. But at a time when the Paris Club of sovereign creditors is increasingly unable to act collectively, the Borrowers’ Platform should ramp up its ambition.
